content: For patients weighing 5 kg or more, administer 25 mg/kg intravenously every 6 hours for non-CNS infections. For patients older than 3 months, the dosage is 15-25 mg/kg intravenously every 6 hours for non-CNS infections, with a maximum daily dose of 2 g for fully susceptible organisms or 4 g for moderately susceptible organisms. For patients older than 12 years, administer 10-15 mg/kg intravenously every 6 hours for mild-to-moderate infections. In patients with cystic fibrosis, the dosage can be increased to a maximum of 100 mg/kg/day intravenously, divided into doses every 6 hours, but should not exceed 4 g/day in older children. This medication is not recommended for pediatric patients with CNS infections due to the risk of seizures. It is also not recommended for pediatric patients weighing less than 30 kg with renal impairment, as no data are available for this population. Drug Interactions: 1. BCG Intravesical Live Vaccine: Imipenem/cilastatin reduces the effectiveness of the BCG intravesical live vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Antimicrobial therapy for other infections may interfere with the effectiveness of the BCG vaccine. Antibiotics with activity against mycobacteria are of particular concern. It is recommended to avoid all antimicrobial therapy during BCG treatment. 2. Cholera Vaccine: Imipenem/cilastatin decreases the effectiveness of the cholera vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration with systemic antibiotics, as these agents may act against the vaccine strain. Do not administer the cholera vaccine to patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 3. Valproic Acid/Divalproex Sodium: Imipenem/cilastatin decreases serum levels of valproic acid by an unknown mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Data suggest that carbapenems may inhibit the hydrolysis of valproic acid glucuronide back to valproic acid, leading to reduced serum concentrations. 4. Ganciclovir: Coadministration with imipenem/cilastatin may increase the risk of seizures. Avoid unless the potential benefit outweighs the risk. 5. Microbiota Oral Therapy: Imipenem/cilastatin reduces the effectiveness of microbiota oral therapy due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Antibiotics may decrease the efficacy of microbiota oral therapy by reducing bacterial spores. Complete antibiotic regimens 2-4 days before initiating microbiota oral therapy. 6. Probenecid: Probenecid increases the levels of imipenem/cilastatin by decreasing renal clearance. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Coadministration increases the plasma level and half-life of imipenem. 7. Sodium Picosulfate: Imipenem/cilastatin decreases the effectiveness of sodium picosulfate by altering metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Antibiotics may reduce the efficacy of sodium picosulfate by altering colonic bacterial flora needed to convert it to its active form. 8. Typhoid Vaccine Live: Imipenem/cilastatin decreases the effectiveness of the typhoid vaccine live due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Postpone administering the vaccine until at least 3 days after completing the antibiotic regimen. 9. Cyclosporine: Cyclosporine may increase the neurotoxic effects of imipenem. Use caution and monitor closely. Case reports describe imipenem increasing or decreasing cyclosporine serum concentration levels. 10. Valacyclovir: Coadministration with imipenem/cilastatin may increase the risk of seizures. Avoid unless the potential benefit outweighs the risk. Precautions: Imipenem/cilastatin is not recommended for use in children with CNS problems due to the risk of seizures. Prolonged use increases the risk of superinfections. Use with caution in patients with renal impairment; adjust dosage in moderate to severe renal dysfunction to avoid the risk of seizures. Carbapenem use may decrease serum levels of valproic acid or divalproex sodium. Combination with aminoglycosides may help combat resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea (CDAD) has been reported and may range in severity from mild diarrhea to fatal colitis. Antibacterial agents can alter the normal flora of the colon, leading to overgrowth of C. difficile. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Available data from a small number of postmarketing cases in pregnancy are insufficient to identify any drug-associated risks for major birth defects, miscarriage, or adverse maternal or fetal outcomes. There is insufficient data on the presence of imipenem/cilastatin in human milk, its effects on the breastfed child, or its effects on milk production. The developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding should be considered alongside the mother’s clinical need for therapy and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed child. Mechanism of Action: Imipenem inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis by binding to penicillin-binding proteins. Cilastatin prevents the renal metabolism of imipenem. The drug is distributed rapidly and widely to most tissues and fluids, including sputum, pleural fluid, peritoneal fluid, interstitial fluid, bile, aqueous humor, reproductive organs, and bone. It crosses the placenta and enters breast milk. Protein binding: Imipenem, 13-21%; Cilastatin, 40%. Administration: Do not administer by IV push. Final concentration should not exceed 5 mg/mL. Infuse ≤500 mg over 20-30 minutes (15-30 minutes in children); infuse >500 mg over 40-60 minutes. If nausea or vomiting occurs during administration, reduce the infusion rate. Reconstituted solutions are stable for 4 hours at room temperature and 24 hours refrigerated (4°C) in normal saline. Normal color ranges from clear to yellow; discard if brown. Side Effects: Common side effects include swelling, redness, pain, or soreness at the injection site. Rarely, it may cause upset stomach, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Serious side effects include severe intestinal conditions caused by C. difficile, which may occur during or weeks to months after treatment. Prolonged or repeated use may result in oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Severe allergic reactions are rare. Missed Dose: It is important to take each dose as scheduled. If a dose is missed, consult your healthcare provider for guidance.
